title: Sifted nerves, finite diagonals, and the geometric realization index
statement:
Use the universes, spaces and infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the simplex category $\Delta$ of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. An infinity category $K$ is sifted when its colimit functor $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)\to\mathcal S$ on spaces preserves finite products. This is equivalent to $K$ being nonempty and its diagonal $K\to K\times K$ being final; final means that restriction preserves colimit cocones of every diagram admitting a colimit. Such $K$ is weakly contractible, meaning its localization at all arrows is equivalent to the one-point space. For each integer $n\geq0$, the finite diagonal $K\to K^n$ is final, including $n=0$ where $K^0$ is the terminal infinity category.

If $K=N(I)$ for a small ordinary category $I$, then $I$ is nonempty and connected and all its finite diagonal functors $I\to I^n$ are final in the ordinary sense: restriction along them preserves ordinary colimits. In particular, for ordinary cocomplete categories $\mathcal C_1,\ldots,\mathcal C_n,\mathcal E$, a functor $F:\prod_{a=1}^n\mathcal C_a\to\mathcal E$ preserving colimits separately, and diagrams $X_a:I\to\mathcal C_a$ for $1\leq a\leq n$, the canonical map
$$\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}F(X_1(i),\ldots,X_n(i))\longrightarrow F(\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}X_1(i),\ldots,\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}X_n(i))$$
is an isomorphism. The same comparison is an equivalence when the categories are cocomplete infinity categories, the $X_a:N(I)\to\mathcal C_a$ are coherent diagrams, and $F$ preserves colimits separately. For $n=0$, the comparison says that the colimit of a constant diagram is its value. Finally $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is sifted, so the preceding assertions apply to geometric realization, namely colimit of a coherent simplicial diagram.
